title: OPTIMISED DEMCARE care home staff training to improve personal care assistance for people living with dementia (feasibility study)
official: Cluster randomised feasibility trial and process evaluation of the OPTIMISED DEMCARE training intervention versus usual care to improve personal care assistance and reduce refusals of care for people with dementia living in care homes 2026-2028
summary:
Background and study aims
People living with moderate and advanced dementia need help with personal care activities such as, washing, dressing and going to the toilet. Sometimes people living with dementia refuse care, which is common in care-home settings. Consequences from refusals include poor hygiene, infections, and use of antipsychotic medication. The study team co-produced a care home staff train-the-trainer training intervention called OPTIMISED DEMCARE to improve personal care assistance for people with dementia in care homes. This study will examine if the training can be tested in a trial situation. The study aims to run a small study of the OPTIMISED DEMCARE training intervention in care homes to determine if a larger trial is feasibility.

Who can participate?
Care home residents living with dementia, and care home staff supporting care home residents living with dementia. The study aims to recruit eight care homes and residents and staff will be living or working in those care homes.

What does the study involve? 
The study will compare the OPTIMISED DEMCARE Training intervention with current care as usual. After care homes have joined the study, residents and staff will be recruited and consent to the study. Family members may be consulted on a resident’s behalf if necessary. Questionnaires will be filled in by staff about their confidence and competence providing dementia care and about residents’ quality of life and refusals of care. Researchers will collect information from resident care records about their recent care. Care homes will then be randomly assigned to receive the OPTIMISED DEMCARE intervention (six care homes) or continue usual care (two care homes). Care home staff in the OPTIMISED DEMCARE Training intervention group will receive an OPTIMISED DEMCARE Pack for inhouse trainers to go through to become DEMCARE Champions. DEMCARE Champions will then train other staff. Staff from all eight care homes will fill in the same questionnaires about themselves and residents again, and researchers will collect information from resident care records, directly after the training period and at 6-months after randomisation.

A number of staff participants in the care homes with the OPTIMISED DEMCARE training will be asked to take part in an interview to find out their views and experiences of the training and being part of this study. Researchers will observe some training sessions.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There are no known benefits. Some people may feel empowered, enjoy taking part and feel good helping researchers. Care home staff and people living with dementia may benefit from the OPTIMISED DEMCARE training, providing and receiving improved personal care assistance and experiencing less refusals of care, although this will not be found out by the current study. Some care homes may use their involvement in research to demonstrate to the Care Quality Commission their outward looking perspective and links with other institutions. There are no known physical risks from taking part. Access to and review of resident care records creates a potential risk to confidentiality. All information about residents will be kept safe and secure. 

Where is the study run from?
The University of East Anglia, Norwich, UK

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
January 2027 to October 2028

Who is funding the study?
An Advanced Fellowship funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), UK.

Who is the main contact?
Dr Tamara Backhouse, Tamara.Backhouse@uea.ac.uk

interventions.name: This is a cluster randomised, feasibility trial incorporating process and economic evaluations comparing the OPTIMISED DEMCARE train-the-trainer intervention against usual care for people living in care homes. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Care homes
1. Situated in England ideally in one of two recruitment regions (East of England and East Midlands) 
2. Registered as specialising in dementia (51% of all care homes) on the CQC website 
3. Manager (and if appropriate,owner / higher management) is prepared to commit to the study
4. Have at least ten residents who meet the resident eligibility criteria

Trial participants: care home staff 
1. Aged 18 and over
2. Work in a study care home regularly,at least 16-hours weekly
3. Providing physical assistance with personal care (for example,washing,dressing,going to the toilet) to people with dementia (e.g.,seniors,carers)
4. Willingness to be trained if their care home is randomised to intervention
*Optional*
5. Willingness to take part in an interview if invited
6. Willingness to be observed during training sessions if invited
7. Willingness to fill in feedback questionnaires about the intervention if applicable

Trial participants: care home residents
1. Aged 18 and over
2. Moderate or advanced stages of dementia (scores of 6 or 7 on FAST (Reisberg,1988) a functional assessment staging tool with seven stages,a score of six represents moderately severe dementia and seven severe dementia).
These residents are likely to have regular physical assistance with personal care.
3. Receiving daily physical assistance with their personal care
4. Living in a participating care home

Process evaluation ONLY participants: care home staff (not participating in the trial)
• Aged 18 or over
• Staff working in an intervention home,receiving or facilitating the training or senior care home staff
• Willingness to fill in feedback questionnaires about the intervention
*Optional*
• Willingness to take part in an interview if invited
• Willingness to be observed during training sessions if invited
Exclusion criteria:
Care homes
1. Participated in dementia training intervention research within the last six-months
2. A refusal of care programme similar to OPTIMISED DEMCARE in place

Trial participants: care home staff
1. Agency staff not working regularly in the care home 
2. Staff not providing assistance with personal care to people with dementia 
3. Taken part in other dementia training research in the last six-months 

Trial participants: care home residents
1. Care-home staff consider the resident at end-of-life - for example,bed care,receiving 2-4-hourly turns and/or mouthcare via swabs and/or sponges 
2. Temporary resident of the care home – for example respite or rehab and reablement residents
3. Not receiving physical assistance with personal care
